title: Why Your Favorite Vegetables Are Disappearing from British Gardens
subtitle: Climate change is forcing gardeners and farmers to rethink what they grow as extreme heat makes traditional crops harder to raise.

summary.en: Recent record-breaking heatwaves in the UK have made it difficult to grow traditional vegetables like cauliflower. The Royal Horticultural Society now advises gardeners to stop planting these thirsty crops. Instead, experts suggest switching to heat-loving plants like tomatoes, okra, and melons. This shift highlights how climate change is changing our food systems and daily habits. Gardeners are now experimenting with new varieties to ensure a successful harvest despite the changing weather.
summary.zh: 英國近期破紀錄的熱浪使得種植花椰菜等傳統蔬菜變得困難。英國皇家園藝學會目前建議園藝愛好者停止種植這些需水量大的作物。專家建議改種番茄、秋葵和甜瓜等喜愛高溫的植物。這種轉變凸顯了氣候變遷如何改變我們的糧食系統與日常生活。園藝愛好者現在正嘗試種植新品種，以確保在變幻莫測的天氣下仍能獲得豐收。

paragraphs.en: For many people in the United Kingdom, a Sunday roast dinner is not complete without a side of cauliflower. However, this classic vegetable is becoming a rare sight in gardens across the country. According to the Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), the UK’s changing climate means that many gardeners should stop trying to grow cauliflower and other related vegetables, such as broccoli and cabbage.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多英國人來說，週日的烤肉大餐若少了花椰菜作為配菜，就不算完整。然而，這種經典蔬菜在全國各地的花園中正變得越來越罕見。根據英國皇家園藝學會（Royal Horticultural Society, RHS）的說法，英國氣候的變遷意味著許多園藝愛好者應該停止嘗試種植花椰菜及其他相關蔬菜，例如青花菜和高麗菜。

paragraphs.en: The reason for this change is the extreme weather the UK has experienced recently. The Met Office, which tracks weather data, reported that this summer was the hottest on record. In August, temperatures in London reached 38.1C. Scientists explain that these intense heatwaves are a direct result of the climate crisis, which is mostly caused by the burning of fossil fuels—materials like coal, oil, and gas used to create energy.
paragraphs.zh: 造成這種變化的原因是英國近期經歷的極端天氣。負責追蹤氣象數據的英國氣象局（Met Office）報告指出，今年夏天是有紀錄以來最熱的一年。八月時，倫敦的氣溫甚至達到攝氏三十八點一度。科學家解釋，這些強烈的熱浪是氣候危機的直接結果，而氣候危機主要是由燃燒化石燃料（如煤炭、石油和天然氣等用於產生能源的物質）所引起的。

paragraphs.en: Cauliflowers belong to a group of plants called brassicas. These plants are known to be "thirsty," meaning they need a lot of water to grow. They also become very stressed when temperatures are high. When it gets too hot, these plants fail to grow a proper head, making them difficult to harvest. Guy Barter, the chief horticulturist at the RHS, noted that these vegetables have been the hardest hit in home gardens. He explained that because summers are likely to stay hot, gardeners should choose different, more resilient plants to save water and ensure a better harvest.
paragraphs.zh: 花椰菜屬於十字花科植物。這類植物以「嗜水」著稱，意味著它們需要大量水分才能生長。同時，當氣溫過高時，它們也會承受極大的壓力。天氣太熱時，這些植物無法長出完整的花球，導致難以收成。英國皇家園藝學會的首席園藝師巴特（Guy Barter）指出，這些蔬菜在家庭花園中受到的衝擊最大。他解釋說，由於夏季可能會持續炎熱，園藝愛好者應該選擇其他更具韌性的植物，以節省用水並確保更好的收成。

paragraphs.en: Many gardeners have already started to change their plans. Simone Bratt, who works at RHS Bridgewater, said she stopped growing cauliflower a few years ago. She explained that the growth was very inconsistent because of the extreme weather. Even when they tried to plant them in the spring, the heat was too much for the young plants. They often "bolted," a term used when a plant grows flowers and seeds too early because of stress, which ruins the vegetable for eating. Bratt suggested that gardeners try growing purple sprouting broccoli instead, as it is better at handling difficult conditions.
paragraphs.zh: 許多園藝愛好者已經開始改變他們的計畫。在英國皇家園藝學會布里奇沃特花園（RHS Bridgewater）工作的布拉特（Simone Bratt）表示，她幾年前就停止種植花椰菜了。她解釋說，由於極端天氣，花椰菜的生長狀況非常不穩定。即使嘗試在春天種植，高溫對幼苗來說也太過強烈。它們經常出現「抽苔」現象，這是指植物因壓力過大而過早開花結籽，導致蔬菜無法食用。布拉特建議園藝愛好者改種紫芽青花菜，因為它更能適應惡劣的環境條件。

paragraphs.en: While some traditional crops are struggling, the changing climate has created new opportunities for other plants. The RHS reported that the recent hot weather has allowed tomatoes and peppers to grow very well outdoors. In some parts of the country, gardeners are even successfully growing melons and watermelons outside, provided they have enough water. Other experts, like Liz Mooney from RHS Garden Wisley, mentioned that cucumbers and sweet potatoes are also growing well in the warmer conditions. Some gardeners have even switched to kale, which has deep roots that help it survive during times of drought—a long period without rain.
paragraphs.zh: 雖然一些傳統作物生長困難，但氣候變遷也為其他植物創造了新機會。英國皇家園藝學會報告稱，近期的炎熱天氣讓番茄和辣椒在戶外生長得非常好。在該國部分地區，只要有足夠的水分，園藝愛好者甚至能成功在戶外種植甜瓜和西瓜。其他專家，如來自英國皇家園藝學會威斯利花園（RHS Garden Wisley）的穆尼（Liz Mooney）提到，小黃瓜和地瓜在較溫暖的環境下也長得不錯。有些園藝愛好者甚至改種羽衣甘藍，這種植物擁有深根，有助於在乾旱（即長期無雨的時期）期間生存。

paragraphs.en: This shift in gardening habits is a sign of a larger problem. Farmers are also facing a poor harvest for many brassica crops this year, with some calling it one of the worst seasons on record. The move away from cauliflower is not just about personal preference; it is a practical response to a world where the weather is becoming less predictable. By choosing plants that are better suited to the heat, gardeners hope to keep their food supply steady.
paragraphs.zh: 這種園藝習慣的轉變是一個更大問題的徵兆。農民今年也面臨許多十字花科作物的歉收，有些人稱這是史上最糟糕的季節之一。放棄種植花椰菜不僅僅是個人喜好的問題，更是對天氣變得越來越難以預測的世界所做出的務實回應。透過選擇更適應高溫的植物，園藝愛好者希望維持穩定的食物供應。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the RHS hopes that recent rains will help winter crops like carrots and leeks recover. However, the trend toward warmer summers means that the vegetables found on British dinner plates will likely continue to change. As people begin to include more heat-loving vegetables like Asian loofah and okra in their meals, the traditional Sunday roast may look quite different in the years to come. The goal for many is to find a balance between keeping old traditions alive and adapting to a new, warmer reality.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，英國皇家園藝學會希望近期的降雨能幫助胡蘿蔔和韭蔥等冬季作物恢復生長。然而，夏季趨於炎熱的趨勢意味著英國餐桌上的蔬菜種類很可能會持續改變。隨著人們開始將更多喜愛高溫的蔬菜（如絲瓜和秋葵）納入餐點，傳統的週日烤肉大餐在未來幾年看起來可能會大不相同。對許多人而言，目標是在維持傳統與適應新的炎熱現實之間找到平衡。

keyTerms.definitionEn: In a state of biological strain or pressure due to unfavorable environmental conditions.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （植物）因環境惡劣而承受壓力，生長受阻。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於描述人的心理狀態，這裡指植物因高溫而生長受阻。文中：They also become very stressed when temperatures are high.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To grow flowers and seeds too early, making the vegetable unsuitable for eating.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （植物）抽苔，指植物因壓力過早開花結籽，導致無法食用。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（衝出、逃跑），這裡指植物生長週期異常。文中：They often "bolted," a term used when a plant grows flowers and seeds too early because of stress, which ruins the vegetable for eating.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Most severely affected by a negative event or situation.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由 hit（擊中）組成的慣用語，這裡指受天氣影響最嚴重。文中：Guy Barter, the chief horticulturist at the RHS, noted that these vegetables have been the hardest hit in home gardens.

quiz.question: According to the article, why do gardeners often fail to harvest a successful cauliflower crop during hot summers?

options.A: The plants require too much fertilizer to survive the heat.
options.B: The plants fail to develop a proper head when temperatures are high.
options.C: The plants are frequently eaten by pests that thrive in warm weather.
options.D: The plants grow too quickly and become too bitter to eat.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第三段明確指出，當氣溫過高時，花椰菜（brassicas）無法長出完整的花球（head），導致難以收成。選項 A 文章未提及肥料問題；選項 C 文章未提到害蟲；選項 D 雖然提到了植物會因為壓力而「抽苔」（bolted），但並非因為長太快導致變苦，而是因為過早開花結籽導致無法食用，與「無法長出花球」是不同的生理現象。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the future of the traditional British Sunday roast?

options.A: It will likely disappear completely as people stop eating vegetables.
options.B: It will become more expensive because imported vegetables are harder to find.
options.C: It will likely feature different types of vegetables than it has in the past.
options.D: It will rely on indoor greenhouse farming to keep traditional crops alive.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章最後一段，作者提到隨著氣候變暖，英國人開始種植並食用如秋葵（okra）等喜熱蔬菜，這暗示了未來餐盤上的內容將會改變，傳統週日烤肉的配菜組成將會與過去不同。選項 A 過於極端，文章僅提到改變而非消失；選項 B 文章未討論進口成本；選項 D 文章強調的是戶外種植的轉變，而非室內溫室農業。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word "bolted" mean in the context of gardening?

options.A: Growing flowers and seeds prematurely due to environmental stress.
options.B: Being physically damaged by strong winds during a storm.
options.C: Being pulled out of the ground by gardeners to save space.
options.D: Growing very slowly because of a lack of nutrients in the soil.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文章第四段明確定義了 "bolted" 一詞，指植物因為壓力（如極端天氣）而過早生長花朵和種子。選項 B 與風災無關；選項 C 是人為動作而非植物的生長狀態；選項 D 描述的是生長緩慢，但 "bolted" 實際上是植物為了繁衍而「過快」進入生殖階段，這會導致蔬菜本身不再適合食用。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article?

options.A: The Royal Horticultural Society is failing to provide enough help to home gardeners.
options.B: Climate change is forcing gardeners to change which crops they grow to adapt to new conditions.
options.C: Cauliflower is becoming a more popular vegetable choice for gardeners in the UK.
options.D: The UK government should ban the use of fossil fuels to protect local gardens.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。全文的核心主旨都在探討英國氣候變遷如何影響園藝，迫使園丁放棄傳統喜涼作物（如花椰菜），轉而種植更適應高溫的作物（如番茄、甜薯），以確保食物來源穩定。選項 A 文章未批評 RHS 的協助；選項 C 與事實相反，花椰菜正變得難以種植；選項 D 雖然提到氣候變遷的成因是化石燃料，但這並非文章討論園藝轉變的主要目的。
